properties.name: mirror_surface gains a REFRESH. FOUND BY RUNNING THE TOOL TWICE, 2026-08-12: a second mirror of the SAME design collided with its own first — 12 of 13 ids refused as collisions, mirrored_edges 0, mirror_content_hash null — leaving the stale node in place with the host edge still pointing at it while `mirrors` reported the OLD pin. So the staleness register read FRESH after a failed refresh, which is worse than never refreshing. Re-mirroring one mirror_of is a DIFFERENT OPERATION from mirroring a new design: replace-what-I-hold-at-a-new-pin versus add-a-stranger-and-refuse-clashes, and only the second existed. THE QUESTION SETTLED FIRST: what happens to a host edge whose foreign target is gone from the new surface? It REFUSES and names both the withdrawn boundary and the host edge pointing at it — reflow2 refuses dangling edges anyway, and a partner retiring a contract you consume is a conversation between two owners, not a cleanup this tool may do (dec:ask-not-repair). A refused refresh changes NOTHING and the pin does not advance, which is the lie the whole fix is about. MECHANISM: the mirrored Project now records `mirror_nodes`, the ids this mirror brought, because the set cannot be recovered afterwards — provenance:imported is also set by corpus ingest, and the project CONTAINS edges do not span the mirrored set (5 of 13, measured). One property on one node type that already carries three mirror properties, following the schema comma-list precedent (pinned/swept on VERIFIES). VERIFIED ON THE REAL PAIR: the exact flo2 scenario that produced the defect now gives 13 nodes, 19 edges, ZERO collisions, refreshed=true, withdrawn naming ifc:reflow2-design-api, the stale node gone and the renamed one present with its corrected medium. 7 tests written first, 4 mutations killed. NOTE FOR THE NEXT RELEASE: adding mirror_nodes moves no stamp count (29/61) but an older binary REFUSES an unknown property — the third instance today of the stamp being blind to a real compatibility event.
